chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah ibn Sinan, from Abu Hamza, from Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) who said:
The oiling (massaging) at night flows in the veins, irrigates the skin, and whitens the face.
ai.seo_question: What are the health and beauty benefits of night oiling according to Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from al-Kafi, Imam al-Baqir (peace be upon him) highlights the prophetic tradition of night-time oiling, emphasizing its physiological benefits such as nourishing the skin and brightening the complexion. This practice is rooted in the broader Shia emphasis on maintaining physical purity and health as a form of worship, reflecting the holistic view of the body in Islamic tradition. The narration underscores the practical wisdom found in the Imams' teachings regarding daily self-care and hygiene.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Yahya, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad Bin Isa, from Ibn Mahboub, from Abdullah Bin Sinan, from Abu Hamza, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The oiling (massaging) at night flows in the veins and it irrigates the person (skin), and whitens the face’.
en.sarwar: 5. Muhammad ibn Yahya has narrated from Ahmad ibn Muhammad ibn ‘Isa from ibn Mahbub ‘Abd Allah ibn Sinan from abu Hamzah who has said the following: “Abu Ja‘far, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
Applied oil at night flows in the veins, quenches the skin and brightens the face.’”
